name: HEAVY BLAST DOORS
text: These thick steel doors haven't opened in
years. The hazard striping is faded, and
whatever machinery once drove them has long
since seized up.

name: SECURITY CHECKPOINT BOOTH
text: A small, cramped booth for whatever poor soul
drew guard duty. The terminal inside still
casts a faint blue glow on the dusty glass.

name: SECURITY CHECKPOINT BOOTH
text: This rusted booth was once the first line of
defense for this facility. The display inside
is cracked but still stubbornly drawing power.

name: INDUSTRIAL LIGHT FIXTURE
text: Twin halogen lamps on a sturdy mast, still
faithfully illuminating the staging area after
all these years.

name: INDUSTRIAL LIGHT FIXTURE
text: These heavy-duty work lights are mounted high
to illuminate the blast doors. The orange glow
feels oddly comforting against the cold steel.

name: THICK RUBBER CABLING
text: Heavy power lines snake out from under the
booth, their rubber casings cracked and stiff
with age.

name: THICK RUBBER CABLING
text: These thick data and power cables connect the
security booth to the main grid, their
protective sheathing brittle from exposure.

name: SANDBAG BARRICADE
text: A hasty defensive line of sandbags, now
petrified into solid lumps by decades of damp
and neglect.

name: SANDBAG BARRICADE
text: These hardened sandbags were placed here to
protect the checkpoint. They're fused
together, crumbling slightly at the edges.

name: RUSTED UTILITY BOX
text: A heavy metal housing for electrical
junctions, stained with streaks of orange
rust.

name: EXTERIOR HVAC UNIT
text: A blocky air exchange unit, its fan silent and
its casing dented. It looks like it was
scavenged from somewhere else and roughly
installed here.

name: EXPOSED CONDUIT BUNDLE
text: Thick power cables spill out from the cracked
flooring, snaking haphazardly toward the
nearby equipment.

name: PILE OF DEBRIS
text: A messy collection of old rags, a crushed
safety cone, and other discarded junk that
blew into this corner.

name: PORTABLE BARRICADE
text: A simple metal frame with hazard striping,
meant to block access to the lower maintenance
areas. It's rusted and slightly bent.
